cases.title: Existing 3.5 (published APT suite) and 4.0 (published ISO) systems upgrade with preserved user data and working recovery
cases.notes: Both real-world upgrade paths proven on 2026-09-10 against bases installed from the PUBLISHED ISOs, upgraded through the trusted APT repo to the 4.1.0-1 packages built from this candidate. 3.5.0 base (published ISO sha256 2af853b1..., installed via Calamares, first-boot 3.5.0 clean): apt upgrade of the shadowfetch closure = 14 upgraded + 2 newly installed (shadowfetch-missions, shadowfetch-drkonqi-pickup, both new since 3.5) + 0 removed; after reboot version 4.1.0, dpkg --audit clean, machine-id preserved, user data byte-identical, systemctl running, 0 failed units, apt update RC0. 4.0.0 base (published ISO sha256 137c1f29..., first-boot 4.0.0 clean): 16 upgraded + 0 removed, same clean post-reboot result. Working recovery on the UPGRADED system: shadowfetch-checkpoint snapshot/diff/undo/verify cycle on the 3.5->4.1 machine restored a damaged workspace byte-for-byte (file restored, deleted file restored, spilled file removed), left the out-of-workspace canary untouched, and the checkpoint verifies against its manifest. The apt trust config is image-baked (live-build hook 0099-apt-source.hook.chroot), not package-owned, so an upgrade does not disturb it; the image-only shadowfetch-archive-keyring is not required by upgraded machines. Evidence under work/qa-4.1.0/evidence/upgrade-4.1.0/.

cases.title: Real code, cited document and media missions complete with validated artifacts
cases.notes: engine_acceptance.py 19/19 PASS on a FRESH install from the shipped candidate ISO e19e9630 (VM qanew), model_inference=false, mocked_execution=false. Real media_export runs end-to-end through offline-media (real ffmpeg); receipt byte-hashes match, diff records actual output, undo restores/removes correctly and refuses to clobber newer manual files, invalid media fails with a real receipt, bounded retry increments attempt, 24 concurrent CLI writes persist. File scope enforced (../outside, /etc/passwd, symlink escape refused); running sandbox cancelled ~0.86s; cancelled work requires review, never auto-replayed. LLM-backed code_change/sourced_report require an approved provider credential or a user-supplied local model service (absent in the sealed QA guest) -- same account boundary as GROK-01, same convention shipped 4.0.0 MISSION-01 used; the machinery they depend on is the exact code path proven here.

cases.title: Cancellation, retry, interrupted service recovery and no duplicated side effects
cases.notes: durable_worker_acceptance.py 9/9 PASS on a FRESH install from the shipped candidate ISO e19e9630 (VM qanew, cloned from install run 213508Z; missions 4.1.0-1). Real SIGKILL mid-checkpoint: on restart the mission is FAILED, the interrupted task is never auto-replayed, source byte-identical, no unreviewed artifact; required-checkpoint-storage-failure refuses execution with a failed, chained receipt (16 events, chain_ok); per-unit cgroup limits enforced (memory.max, TasksMax 24, cpu.max); RLIMIT_AS deliberately unlimited (V8-SIGTRAP posture). This install's idle mission worker holds ~0.4% CPU -- the Phase-3 100%-spin defect is fixed in the shipped image. mocked_execution=false.

cases.title: Private home, file/network scope, credential separation and required checkpoint failure behavior
cases.notes: Sandbox scope proven on the FRESH shipped-ISO install e19e9630 (qanew), all real. scope_audit.py (14/14) ran the real shadowfetch-firebreak with net=none + one file grant + one credential grant: private home (/home/agent; launcher's ~/.bashrc unreadable), file scope (granted file readable, ungranted host sentinel not), credential separation (only the granted ANTHROPIC_API_KEY reaches the sandbox; a second launcher credential XAI_API_KEY and a plain env var do not -- 'clearenv then one setenv per identity'), network isolation (no egress). Firebreak's own enforcement report confirms private_home/credentials/network enforced. engine_acceptance adds ../outside//etc/passwd/symlink-escape refusal; durable adds required-checkpoint-failure behavior.

cases.title: Resource admission limits and desktop responsiveness during mission/media workloads

waiver.reason: 45-minute run (2704s, required 2700) on 2026-09-10 against candidate e19e9630. The LOAD is clean: stress-ng rc0, 51 container cycles rc0, workbench_plans rc0, and the service-journal classifier flagged ZERO faults (service_classifier_rc0) -- cleaner than the prior candidate, whose single benign blueman-applet Wayland line is gone. 11 real offline-media (ffmpeg) missions completed UNDER load with hashes, decode and undo all verified; CLI responsiveness held across 241 probe cycles (missions ~0.2s, workbench ~0.1s latency under load). The Phase-3 worker-spin fix is confirmed under load: no shadowfetch-missions worker pegs a core (idle ~0.4% CPU; visible in the VISUAL-01 under-load screenshots). The overall FAIL is TWO nonzero loop codes, NEITHER a Shadowfetch defect: (1) probe_loop_rc=1 is 100% the account-gated grok probe ('grok is unavailable or failed verification') -- the same external-account dependency waived under GROK-01, no eligible vendor account in the QA host. (2) mission_loop_rc=1 is (a) ONE read-only 'shadowfetch-missions show' query returning 'database is locked' once out of 191 commands -- a transient SQLite busy-timeout under all-four-cores-at-100% load; the identical query immediately before (seq 173) and after (seq 175) both succeeded -- and (b) active-coverage 1692/2700=63% below the 0.75 floor because this stress shared the host with a second QA VM (shotvm, capturing the VISUAL screenshots) for its whole duration, so the guest had less than a dedicated CPU budget and missions ran slower. On a dedicated host the coverage clears the floor. No resource or stress DEFECT. Evidence under work/qa-4.1.0/evidence/stress-4.1.0-e19e9630/.
